page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is a virtual machine type within the Daldv6 series, architected for compute-centric workloads that benefit from integrated fast local disk storage. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and utilizes an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz. Provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading, the system includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per cluster. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI.

The server is provisioned with 96.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a reduced memory profile of 2.0 GB per vCPU relative to typical general-purpose instances. Ephemeral storage is bundled directly via 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, avoiding network storage latency for intermediate files. The configuration contains zero discrete GPUs, focusing entirely on x86_64 CPU computation and high-speed local disk operations.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate upper-quartile compute capability. The instance recorded strong results in stress-ng multi-core testing (73,858.94) and Geekbench multi-core scoring (20,503.0), alongside 47,917.0 in Clang software compilation. Database and key-value evaluations revealed 66.39 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and a PassMark database score of 22,486.11. While cached read bandwidth reached 3,648.29 GB/sec, uncached read and write throughput measured in the average range at 113.58 GB/sec and 83.36 GB/sec, respectively. Small model LLM inference generation performed in the top tier at 339.07 tokens per second, but generation speed fell to lower tiers on large 70B parameter models due to RAM constraints and CPU-only execution.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D48alds_v6 offers strong compute density per resource unit for applications that do not require extensive memory overhead. The inclusion of 2,832 GB local NVMe SSD storage makes the platform particularly effective for CI/CD code compilation, high-concurrency batch processing, transient data transformation, Redis caching layers, and search indexing jobs requiring rapid scratch disk space.
description: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is a compute-aligned virtual machine configuration within the Daldv6 family, designed for processing-heavy workloads that require fast local disk I/O. The instance delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 vector instruction sets. Memory is provisioned at 96 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation. Storage is directly integrated with 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while discrete GPU hardware is omitted. Benchmark results indicate top-quartile performance in multi-core execution, PassMark CPU tests, Clang compilation, and Redis key-value operations. The system presents an efficient compute profile for parallel batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, staging databases, and distributed caching systems.
